svg.aria-label: How to write ಷ: 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 7 movements
svg.title: Writing ಷ
svg.desc: 7 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ಷ (kannada), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansKannada-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-shha.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಷ, 40 frames, 4.0 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016) <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kannada-alphabet-shha.gif>. Source note on variation: The CC BY-SA 4.0 animation writes ಷ in four pen-down runs: from the inner tip of the curl the pen winds up and round to the left, runs along the base, rises into the middle point, drops round the right lobe and climbs the right side, curving over at the top (frames 0–12); after a lift, the dot in the middle (frame 13); after a second lift, the top bar from left to right curling up into the hook (frames 14–20); after a third lift, the slanting stroke from above the right lobe down across it to the lower right (frames 21–24). Its body is ಪ's. The frames were read from a mirror copy that matches the Commons file's listed size (268×227, 119 KB) and byte size. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Kannada outline rather than copying the animation's handwritten proportions; in that outline the dot is a filled disc, drawn as a small closed loop inside it, and the slanting stroke is a straight bar, which the path follows, but the three-lift order remains the same.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 7 movements
Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-shha.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಷ, 40 frames, 4.0 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
